items.name: Give

clay_stages.description: Clay in the Potter's Hands — our picture of personal spiritual growth, from Isaiah 64:8. Five ordered stages, each multiplying something.

primary.name: Brand Leaf Green
primary.usage: Primary brand green on light backgrounds. This is the canonical application-palette green — used for layouts, backgrounds, accents, CSS tokens, website styling, and newly created branded materials. It is deliberately distinct from the green(s) embedded in official logo artwork (see logos.lockups colors and the note below) — the two do not need to match exactly. Rules, large kickers, accents, buttons, icon fills. As a text color it only reaches WCAG AA at large-text sizes (see color_system.accessibility) — for small text and labels use Green Deep instead, and when this green is a solid background behind text, set the text in Ink (#221f1b), not white.

tones.name: Green Deep
tones.usage: Small text, links, and labels on light backgrounds where #5f9a32 lacks contrast. Passes WCAG AA for normal text on Paper.

tones.name: Green Bright
tones.usage: Accent green for DARK backgrounds only. Canonical application-palette green for dark backgrounds — see the note above about logo artwork carrying its own, separate green. Never on paper — fails contrast badly at any text size on light backgrounds.

secondary.name: Olive
secondary.usage: Muted supporting green. Scripture rules, eyebrow labels, the road motif.

tones.name: Olive Deep
tones.usage: Dark green panels and contrast columns with white text.

neutral_dark.name: Charcoal
neutral_dark.usage: Dark backgrounds — covers, section dividers, action slides. See color_system.rules for the pure-black policy.

neutral_light.name: Paper
neutral_light.usage: Primary light background. Warm off-white. See color_system.rules for the pure-white policy.

tones.name: Paper Card
tones.usage: Cards, wells, and inset panels on light backgrounds.

ink.usage: Primary body and heading text on light backgrounds.

metadata.usage: Small uppercase labels, tags, and swatch metadata on light backgrounds (Paper, Paper Card, or white) where ink_soft reads as too heavy. Passes WCAG AA for normal text against all three.

metadata_on_dark.usage: Small uppercase labels and metadata on Charcoal backgrounds where on_dark reads as too heavy. Passes WCAG AA for normal text against Charcoal.

hairline.usage: Dividers and card borders on light backgrounds.

accents.description: Four earthy, green-anchored accent colors used to differentiate categories and sections. They happen to color-code the On-Ramps framework (frameworks.on_ramps) in Gather/Give/Group/Go order, but should be referred to by color name — Moss, Teal, Ochre, Terracotta — everywhere outside that specific framework. Never introduce a fifth.

moss.name: Moss Green
moss.usage: As a solid background, neither white nor Ink passes WCAG AA for normal-size text (both land around 4.0:1). Safe for large text (18pt+/14pt bold+, roughly 24px+), for the swatch name treatment, or as a border, rule, icon, or other decorative/non-text element. For normal-size text, use Moss Deep instead — either as the text color on a light background, or set small text inside a light chip rather than directly on the Moss fill.

tones.name: Moss Deep
tones.usage: Small text, labels, and links on light backgrounds where Moss (#5d8a3e) lacks contrast. Passes WCAG AA for normal text on Paper.

teal.name: Muted Teal
teal.usage: Passes WCAG AA for normal text both as a background with white text and as a text color on Paper.

ochre.name: Ochre
ochre.usage: As a solid background, Ink passes WCAG AA for normal text; white does not (3.3:1) and is large-text only. As a text color on light backgrounds, Ochre itself fails normal-text contrast — use Ochre Deep instead.

tones.name: Ochre Deep
tones.usage: Small text, labels, and links on light backgrounds where Ochre (#b3852b) lacks contrast. Passes WCAG AA for normal text on Paper.

terracotta.name: Terracotta
terracotta.usage: Passes WCAG AA for normal text both as a background with white text and as a text color on Paper.

interactive.description: For on-screen product UI only — logged-in app-like screens, buttons, links, hover states, and small badges on very dark backgrounds, as used on my.nvf.life. Print, booklets, announcement graphics, and other static compositions should keep using the palette and accents above, not these. This tier exists because tiny interactive elements need more lightness and chroma than a printed page does to stay legible and tappable against a near-black screen.

surface_dark.name: UI Charcoal
surface_dark.usage: Primary dark background for app-like screens — a touch darker than Charcoal for extra contrast against the brighter interactive greens below.

link.name: Interactive Green
link.usage: Links and secondary interactive text on dark UI.

button.name: Interactive Green, Bold
button.usage: Primary buttons and other high-emphasis controls on dark UI.

alert.name: Alert Red
alert.usage: Errors, destructive actions, and required-field warnings. The only red in the system — reserve it for real alerts, never decoration.

badge_teal.name: Badge Teal
badge_teal.usage: Small tags and badges on dark UI, where Muted Teal needs more lift to read at tiny sizes.

badge_ochre.name: Badge Ochre
badge_ochre.usage: Small tags and badges on dark UI, where Ochre needs more lift to read at tiny sizes.

accessibility.description: Verified WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text — 18pt/24px+ regular or 14pt/18.66px+ bold) for every meaningful text/background pairing in this system. 'normal' means safe for body copy, small labels, and small uppercase tracked text. 'large_only' means safe only at large-text sizes — do not use for body copy, captions, or small labels. 'decorative_only' means the pairing does not clear even the large-text minimum and must not carry any text — border, rule, icon, or fill use only. Standard is WCAG 2.1 Level AA.

Green Deep as text on Paper.
Green Bright as text on Charcoal.
Green Bright on Paper. Fails even the large-text minimum — never use on light backgrounds, per color_system.rules.

Moss Deep as text on Paper.

Teal as text on Paper.
White text on Ochre background — large text only.
Ink text on Ochre background — the correct default pairing.

rules: Never use pure black or pure white as general background colors. Use Charcoal and Paper instead. Pure black or white may remain where it is part of approved, unmodified logo artwork or required one-color reproduction.

On light backgrounds use Brand Leaf Green (#5f9a32) or Green Deep (#42701f). On dark backgrounds switch to Green Bright (#74ca33). These are the canonical application-palette greens — distinct from, and not required to match, whatever green is embedded in a given piece of official logo artwork.
Greens lead. The four accent colors differentiate categories. Warm neutrals carry everything else.
Limit any single composition to one or two background colors.
Avoid neon colors and heavy saturated primaries — keep every hue warm and slightly desaturated.
Never use color_system.interactive in print or static compositions. It exists only for on-screen product UI.

Before pairing any text color with any background color, check color_system.accessibility.pairings. Never place normal-size text in a pairing classified large_only or prohibited. If a pairing you need is not listed, calculate the WCAG 2.1 contrast ratio rather than guessing.

display.usage: All headings, titles, labels, kickers, numbers, and UI. Tight letter-spacing (-0.01em to -0.028em) on large headings; wide tracking (0.12em to 0.34em) on small uppercase labels.

body.usage: All long-form and body copy. Line-height approximately 1.4 to 1.6. Apply text-wrap: pretty.

script.usage: Warm human accents only — a greeting, a value name, a caption lead-in such as 'We are…'. Never for body copy or critical information. One flourish per composition.

display_alternates.description: Used only in the On-Ramp cover lockup, set in Canva. Not required for general brand work.

scale.note: Sizes are expressed for a 1920x1080 canvas. Scale proportionally for other media. For print, body copy sits between 12pt and 15pt.

minimums.projection_note: For projected media, minimum text size is viewing_distance / 200. At 40 feet that is 2.4 inches. Never smaller.

typography.license_note: Fonts are provided by their respective sources. Follow the source's current terms when downloading or distributing them. See each family's source field above for its direct Google Fonts page.

md.usage: Cards, wells, and inset panels. The default.

lg.usage: Large panels on projected or oversized media.

rules: Prefer SVG for all vector and programmatic use.
Match the variant to the background. Every asset entry carries a use_on field and a colors array — read them before placing a logo.
On light backgrounds use the color variant (charcoal wordmark). On dark or photographic backgrounds use color_on_dark or white — the charcoal wordmark will not read.
Maintain clearspace equal to the height of the leaf mark on all sides.
Never stretch, recolor, rotate, add effects to, or place the logo on a busy background without a darkening veil.

The green(s) embedded in each logo asset (see each asset's colors field) are immutable, asset-specific logo colors, not the application palette. They do not need to match color_system.palette.primary or Green Bright exactly, and must never be edited to match them. Official logo artwork must always be used exactly as supplied.
The stacked lockup is the default choice. Reach for the horizontal wordmark only when vertical space is constrained.
The horizontal wordmark has an aspect ratio of roughly 22:1. In constrained layouts, size it by width and never let it crowd adjacent navigation or type.

For the horizontal wordmark: all_black and all_white are single-color, no green — use where the design needs one flat ink. white_text and black_text both keep the green leaf mark, differing only in the wordmark color for light vs. dark backgrounds.

voice.summary: New Vision sounds warm, grounded, and hopeful. We are inviting people into something bigger than themselves, so we open doors rather than push. Grace and truth are not rivals — we say hard things kindly and clearly, never hedging them into vagueness. Plain language carries profound ideas. Concrete detail earns trust where superlatives do not. Every piece points to one clear next step.
voice.statement: Write like a trusted friend who is a little further down the road: warm, direct, unhurried. Invite people in — never recruit, pressure, or hype. Use plain words for deep things, and say hard truths kindly and clearly. Be specific: real names, real numbers, real next steps. Write to 'you' in active voice, mostly short sentences, with one warm flourish per piece.
do: Choose the shorter, plainer word; explain any church term a guest would not know
Be specific — real names, real numbers, real streets earn trust
Invite warmly: 'There's a seat for you here'
Say hard truths kindly and plainly; never soften them into vagueness
End with one concrete next step: verb, what happens, where to go
Keep sentences mostly short; read aloud and cut anything breathless
Use Title Case for titles, ALL CAPS for short labels, sentence case elsewhere
Add exactly one warm human flourish per piece
Keep paragraphs to one idea, three or four sentences maximum
dont: No urgency or FOMO — avoid 'don't miss out', 'limited time', 'last chance'
No hype words: amazing, incredible, life-changing, unlock
No corporate speak: leverage, utilize, engagement, onboarding, stakeholders
No insider shorthand used cold — unpacking, doing life, pouring into, seasons
No hedging with just, kind of, sort of, maybe
Never imply anyone is behind, failing, or missing out by not participating
Do not write about 'people' in third person when you mean the reader
Do not substitute superlatives for evidence — show the number instead
No more than one script flourish or exclamation point per piece
Never use straight quotes or apostrophes; always use curly
example_phrases: There's a seat for you here.
Let's get moving for the Master.
Serving isn't the finish line, it's the starting line.
Grace and truth are not rivals.
If you can find us, you can worship with us.

ai_content_rules.description: Rules for any AI agent drafting New Vision copy, on top of the voice object above. These protect against confidently-wrong output — invented facts read as authoritative and are hard to catch after the fact.
never_invent: Event dates, times, prices, registration details, or locations
Facts about actual members, photographs, or events
ai_content_rules.when_info_is_missing: Ask a concise clarifying question rather than guessing. If the author explicitly asks for an incomplete draft anyway, use a visible placeholder such as [NEEDS EVENT DATE], list every unresolved placeholder at the end, and never represent the draft as publication-ready.

scripture.preferred_translation: NASB 2020, unless the author specifies otherwise. NASB95, CSB, and ESV are also acceptable in some cases when the author requests them.
scripture.never_invent_wording: Use the exact text supplied by the author, or text verified from an authorized source. If the wording cannot be verified, either ask the author for the passage text or cite the reference only, without quoting it.
scripture.always_identify_translation: Always name the translation (usually NASB 2020) when quoting Scripture.

human_review_required_for: Claims about real people or events
Potentially misleading AI imagery — see ai_imagery

kicker_lockup.description: The recurring section-header motif. A small uppercase green kicker, then a large Archivo title, then a short rule bar.
kicker_lockup.spec: Kicker: Archivo 800, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.26em, primary green. Title: Archivo 900, tight tracking. Rule: 104px wide, 7px tall, rounded, primary green.

card.spec: Background Paper Card (#f1ece2), radius 10-20px, generous padding, and frequently a 5-14px left or top accent border in the category color.

contrast_columns.description: Two side-by-side columns used to contrast ideas — one light, one dark.
contrast_columns.spec: Left column Paper Card with ink-soft text. Right column Olive Deep (#37461f) with white text and inline bold Green Bright highlights on key phrases.

image_veil.description: The treatment that makes white text legible over photography.
image_veil.spec: Place a bottom-weighted linear gradient over the image: rgba(36,32,29,0.15) at 0%, rgba(36,32,29,0.05) at 38%, rgba(36,32,29,0.60) at 72%, rgba(36,32,29,0.88) at 100%. Set caption text in white Archivo 900 with a Kaushan Script lead-in above it in Green Bright.
image_veil.warning: Do not use blurred text-shadow for legibility. Print and PDF engines rasterize large-blur shadows into visible rectangles. Use the gradient veil instead.

road_motif.description: A winding road on dark asphalt, used on covers and back covers to carry the On-Ramp metaphor.
road_motif.spec: Dark charcoal radial base, an olive green road path with a dashed center line, and a subtle noise texture. Always veiled before type is placed on it.

timeline.spec: A vertical spine with a gradient from primary green to olive, the year on the left in Archivo 900 green, and alternating filled and outlined dots on the line. Dots sit above the spine.

photography.description: Direction for any photograph, video still, or AI-generated image produced for New Vision — booklets, announcements, web, or anything else. Independent of any single project.
photography.mood: Warm, cinematic, editorial — grounded, hopeful, and premium, like a well-made print piece. Never garish, clip-arty, or corporate-stock.
photography.lighting: Golden-hour warmth and soft natural light, with a gentle film grain. Slightly desaturated, warm-leaning color grade. Charcoal shadows, never crushed to pure black. Cinematic but understated — no HDR, no harsh contrast.

motifs.name: Road
motifs.note: A winding or open road, the journey of faith. See brand_elements.road_motif for the graphic treatment — the same idea applies to photography.

motifs.name: Leaf and new growth
motifs.note: A single leaf or a fresh sprout, echoing the leaf mark. Visual shorthand for growth.

motifs.name: Pottery and clay
motifs.note: Earthen vessels, hands shaping or holding clay, kiln-fired pottery. Our picture of formation, from Isaiah 64:8 — see frameworks.clay_stages. The vessel and the material carry the meaning; a literal potter's wheel in motion is not required.

motifs.name: Hands
motifs.note: Open, giving, or raised in worship.

motifs.name: Community
motifs.note: People gathered, walking together, going out into neighborhoods and nations — Acts 2:41-47.

photography.composition: Clean and minimal, generous negative space, a strong focal subject at shallow depth of field. When a shot will carry a text overlay, keep roughly one third of the frame open and darker for it — see brand_elements.image_veil for the treatment that finishes the job.
photography.subject_tone: Real, candid, diverse, and intergenerational people — never stocky, staged, or generic stock photography of people who are not our people. Authentic worship, service, and hospitality. Reverent and joyful, never cheesy.
photography.one_liner: Warm, cinematic, editorial photography in a charcoal-and-green palette — golden light, open roads, growing and shaped things, and authentic community — with minimalist composition and room for clean modern type.

ai_imagery.description: Rules specific to AI-generated or materially AI-altered imagery, on top of the general photography direction above.
ai_imagery.internal_record: Keep an internal record whenever final, published imagery is AI-generated or materially AI-altered — what was generated, and for what piece.
ai_imagery.public_disclosure: Publicly disclose AI use whenever a reasonable viewer might mistake the image for a real New Vision person, event, facility, ministry activity, mission trip, testimony, or historical moment.
never: Portray a generated person as an actual member, guest, employee, missionary, ministry recipient, or community resident.
Create an identifiable depiction of a real person without that person's permission.
Generate an image of a minor that implies it documents an actual New Vision activity.
Use AI to recreate, repair, extend, redesign, or otherwise regenerate any logo in this kit — see governance.logo_modification_policy.
Leave conceptual or illustrative AI imagery unlabeled where the surrounding context could mislead a viewer into thinking it is documentary.
ai_imagery.style_direction: Any AI-generated image must still follow the photography object above for mood, lighting, motifs, composition, and subject tone — AI imagery is not a separate visual style.

digital_signage.description: A high-impact, read-from-a-distance visual language — bold type, dark charcoal backgrounds, a photo, minimal clutter. Born on the roadside digital sign, but the same mood, typography, motifs, and motion also carry to Sunday-morning presentation slides (1920x1080) and, for some announcements, Facebook/Instagram posts. It is not the definitive design for slides or social — just one strong, on-brand option for them. Shares the mood, palette, and subject_tone of the photography object above, but with its own typography and motion rules specific to this family of high-impact formats. Not for print or general web.

extended_dark_shades.description: Additional near-black tones for high-contrast, read-from-a-distance use. Use alongside Charcoal (#24201d), not as a replacement for it in other contexts.

digital_signage.typography: Archivo at its heaviest weight (900) is the default, mostly uppercase with tight line spacing and strong left alignment — do not use thin weights for main text. When a design calls for an even more condensed, distance-legible headline than Archivo provides, approved alternates are Anton, Bebas Neue, League Spartan, Montserrat ExtraBold, Oswald Heavy, or a Druk-style condensed face — used sparingly, not as a replacement for Archivo elsewhere in the brand. Off-white text on dark; green reserved for emphasis words only. Accent text may use small uppercase tracked-out labels, or — sparingly — a single warm handwritten phrase in Kaushan Script.

layout.description: The composition principles below are shared across formats; the exact split is specific to the roadside sign's wide canvas. On other canvases, keep the same feel — dominant text, one supporting photo, a dark gradient for legibility, generous negative space — but adapt the split to the aspect ratio rather than forcing 2:1.
layout.roadside_sign: A wide, roughly 2:1 billboard composition. Left 55-65% carries the large headline; right 35-45% carries the photographic subject. A dark gradient overlay runs left to right so the text stays readable.
layout.sunday_slides: 1920x1080 (16:9) presentation slides. The same dark, bold, text-forward feel, but composed for a widescreen frame rather than the sign's 2:1 split — e.g. text over a full-bleed photo with a gradient veil, or a top/bottom split instead of left/right.
layout.social_posts: For select Facebook/Instagram announcements only, not every post. Adapt the same mood and typography to the platform's own canvas (square or vertical) rather than the sign's proportions.
layout.shared: No more than one photo, no icon clutter, generous negative space. The logo, if used, sits small-to-medium in a corner as an exact flat asset only — never redrawn, distorted, or rearranged.

digital_signage.background_motifs: Large, very faint two-leaf shape in dark green or olive; a soft green gradient glow; thin green accent lines; subtle dust or grain texture; an occasional very faint hexagon or geometric pattern; a warm vignette at the edges; charcoal paper texture.

motion.description: For any animated / video version of a signage slide.
motion.entrance: Text enters word-by-word with a quick scale-up-and-settle 'stomp' — slight overshoot, then lock into place. Words appear one at a time over 0.4-0.8 seconds total.
motion.layers: Background leaf motif slides or fades in subtly from the left. The photo layer slides in from the right, beneath the text. Light parallax between the background, photo, and text layers. A single green accent line or glow sweeps across once.
motion.constants: Gentle film grain or texture remains constant throughout.
motion.avoid: No animation of the people themselves. No bouncing, spinning, or excessive effects.
motion.timing: Hold the completed slide long enough for easy reading. Transitions between slides are smooth, dark, and understated.

digital_signage.one_liner: A bold, high-impact ministry-values look using authentic church photography, large readable typography, dark charcoal backgrounds, green brand accents, subtle leaf motifs, and cinematic editorial motion — born on the roadside sign, at home on Sunday slides and select social posts too — communicating clarity, warmth, conviction, mission, and community.

do: Use warm neutrals, confident large headings, and generous whitespace
Color-code categories with the four accent colors
Pair real photography with the gradient veil for text legibility
Lead sections with the kicker-title-rule lockup
Use flex or grid with gap for all sibling layout
dont: No aggressive gradient backgrounds or glassmorphism

Never use pure black or pure white as general background colors. Use Charcoal and Paper instead. Pure black or white may remain where it is part of approved, unmodified logo artwork or required one-color reproduction.
No competing accent colors beyond the defined four
Do not use Inter, Roboto, or Arial — the Archivo and Source Serif 4 pairing is the signature

print.description: There is no single fixed trim size, bleed, resolution, or color mode for New Vision print work — those depend on the specific piece and the specific printer. Past versions of this file listed one project's numbers (Letter-size, 350 DPI, CMYK) as if they were universal; they were not.
print.note: Before sending any file to print, ask the printer for that job's trim size, bleed, minimum resolution, color mode, and accepted file format, and design to those numbers. Do not assume 350 DPI, CMYK, or Letter trim unless the printer for that specific job confirms them.

rules: Start with this file. It is the single machine-readable source of truth for New Vision Fellowship's brand. See $schema / schema_version for the file's structure, and governance.brand_steward for who to ask when something here is unclear or missing.
Resolve every asset path against base_url. All paths are relative to the repository root.

Use Brand Leaf Green (#5f9a32) as the primary color on light backgrounds and Green Bright (#74ca33) on dark ones — these are the canonical application-palette colors for layouts, backgrounds, accents, CSS tokens, website styling, and new branded materials. Official logo artwork carries its own, separately-set green(s) (see each asset's colors field) that do not need to match this palette and must never be edited to match it — use logo files exactly as supplied. Before pairing any color with text, check color_system.accessibility.pairings; do not assume white-on-brand-green or white-on-Ochre is safe for normal-size text — it is not.
Set all headings in Archivo and all body copy in Source Serif 4. Use Kaushan Script only for a single warm accent per composition.
Prefer the stacked logo lockup. Match the variant to the background using each asset's use_on field: color on light, color_on_dark or white on dark.
Follow the voice object for all copy. Read brand-guidelines.md for the full tone and usage rules.
For any photography or AI-generated imagery, follow the photography object for mood, lighting, motifs, composition, and subject tone, and follow ai_imagery for disclosure and consent rules.

For the roadside digital sign, Sunday-morning presentation slides, or a high-impact social announcement, follow the digital_signage object instead — it overrides typography and layout for that family of formats. It is not the only option for slides or social, just a strong on-brand one.
There is no fixed universal trim size, bleed, DPI, or color mode for print — see the print object and ask the printer for that job's specifications before designing to them.

For NC Baptists, SBC, IMB, NAMB, Triad Church Network, Who's Your One, or ServeNC, read outside_partnerships instead of sub_brands or initiatives. Never reproduce their logos here — link out to each entry's resources field for their own official assets.

Never redraw, trace, vectorize, recolor, distort, or AI-recreate any logo in this kit. If a format you need does not exist in logos/, sub-brands/, or initiatives/, ask for it rather than approximating it — see governance.logo_modification_policy.

Before writing any copy, read ai_content_rules. Never invent service times, event details, staff names, contact information, statistics, testimonies, or ministry claims — ask a clarifying question instead, or mark an intentionally incomplete draft with visible placeholders.
